distractors.reason: 'Fluent' is an adjective, so it cannot modify the verb 'speak'. We need an adverb: speak fluently.
'Fluency' is a noun. It names the ability and cannot describe how someone speaks.
'Fluid' describes smooth movement or liquids. It is not used with 'speak' in this sense.

example_sentence: She can speak English ___ after two years abroad.
l1_interference: Türkçe'de zarf genellikle fiilden önce gelir, bu yüzden öğrenciler 'fluently speak' ya da 'speak fluent' gibi yanlış kalıplar kurabilir. İngilizce'de ise zarf fiilin arkasına gelir.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually follows the verb in this collocation: speak fluently, listen carefully, work hard. Adjectives like 'fluent' describe nouns, while adverbs describe verbs.

related_collocations.example: Please listen carefully to the instructions.
She had to work hard to pass the exam.
I did not sleep well last night.

memory_tip: Turkish puts the adverb before the verb (akıcı konuşmak); English puts it after the verb (speak fluently).
